profileContract.rationale: The plan will assign client UI, networking, shop catalog, economy, escrow, persistence, commands, configuration, and release ownership across both support lines.
Stable request identities, integer value movement, exact NBT identity, atomic writes, reproducible fixtures, exact revision tests, deterministic audits, and repeatable candidate hashes are mandatory.

The plan will distinguish validation, readiness, authorization, inventory, custody, persistence, recovery, network, configuration, dependency, external evidence, and publication failures with fail closed behavior and actionable evidence.

profileContract.plan_section: Scope generalization and bounded extension rules
profileContract.rationale: The rolling defect policy applies a common deduplicated issue, repair, and verification workflow, while issue 33 remains a deliberately bounded reusable catalog operation rather than an unbounded query language.
The plan will define GitHub issue evidence, catalog selections, inventory and transaction inputs, UI and command outputs, reporter evidence, and exact candidate artifacts.
The endpoint is verified merged support branches and exact beta candidate artifacts, while platform publication, stable release, and announcements remain excluded until separately authorized.
The plan requires a complete audit and repair pass for leaks, backdoors, packet and command trust, secrets, paths, deserialization, permissions, duplication, privacy, and dependency packaging.

A codebase wide persistence audit is mandatory and includes every journal, checkpoint, ledger, custody store, claim store, SavedData object, inventory proof, NBT record, JSON and TOML file, migration, atomic write, backup, reload, concurrency, integrity, recovery, and corruption path.

The plan will require focused regressions, full tests, data validation, GameTests, builds, server and client smoke tests, controlled multiplayer, restart, reconnect, fault injection, reporter acceptance, and exact revision evidence.
The owner locked Forge 1.20.1 to 3.0.0-beta.2 and NeoForge 1.21.1 to 2.2.1, with fixes integrated only into their correct support branches.

optionalFutureScope.summary: Publish the prepared artifacts to CurseForge, Modrinth, or GitHub Releases and post an announcement after a separate explicit authorization.
Promote either support line from beta or maintenance candidate status to a stable public release.
Add material unrelated enhancements or new subsystems that are not required by an active defect, issue 33, or a verified audit defect.
Extend bulk selection to fuzzy item matching, arbitrary NBT paths, broad tag expression languages, or unconditional replacement policies.
Support distributed live market state across multiple servers or direct external storage listings without deterministic transaction receipts.

nonGoals.summary: Do not implement product code, modify tracked repository files, or perform release operations during the Plan Creator pass.
Do not publish to CurseForge, Modrinth, GitHub Releases, announce a release, or declare stable status under this plan endpoint.
Do not delete player data, journals, checkpoints, ledgers, custody, claims, or worlds as a repair or verification strategy.

Do not weaken server authority, maintenance mode, readiness checks, escrow conservation, request idempotency, claims access, permissions, or dedicated server safety to make a UI path appear available.
Do not merge Forge fixes into the NeoForge support line or NeoForge fixes into the Forge support line without an independently required compatible implementation.
Do not add fuzzy matching, arbitrary NBT query paths, unconditional bulk replacement, or a second competing item selector for issue 33.
Do not close an issue because a patch compiles, a mocked test passes, or an external suggestion exists when the required real behavior evidence is absent.
Do not silently update Minecraft, Forge, NeoForge, Java, mappings, Gradle, or other pinned platform boundaries as part of defect repair.

ownerDecisions.question: What exact endpoint constitutes completion for this polish plan?
ownerDecisions.selectedChoice: All scoped and audit discovered repository owned defects are fixed, merged on the correct support branch, fully verified, accepted where reporter evidence is mandatory, and closed. Both exact beta candidate artifacts are prepared and proven. Public platform releases, stable publication, and announcements remain excluded until later explicit authorization.
ownerDecisions.rationale: Completion means a trustworthy candidate state, not only locally compiling patches.

ownerDecisions.question: Does the plan cover only issues open at intake or defects found during execution?
ownerDecisions.selectedChoice: Scope rolls forward for verified defects. Every discovered defect is deduplicated and filed on GitHub before repair, then fixed and verified. A repeated final audit at exact candidate revisions must find no remaining known repository owned defect. Material unrelated enhancements require a later explicit Plan Creator revision.
ownerDecisions.rationale: The owner selected convergence on a clean known-defect set instead of freezing scope to the intake snapshot.

ownerDecisions.question: What is the bounded behavior for the issue 33 bulk listing workflow?
ownerDecisions.selectedChoice: Reuse the searchable grid for bounded registry selection, allow optional one exact canonical NBT identity, show a full generated listing preview, apply one shared price and stock through one atomic catalog write, skip and report existing listings by default, and require explicit per item replacement that preserves unrelated fields. Exclude fuzzy matching, arbitrary NBT paths, and unconditional replacement.
ownerDecisions.rationale: This gives administrators fast bulk entry without creating an ambiguous query or destructive replacement system.

ownerDecisions.question: How should missing issue evidence and reporter acceptance affect execution and closure?
ownerDecisions.selectedChoice: Preserve and request exact non destructive evidence. If evidence is unavailable, use the authenticated EnVisione GitHub account to tag the issue author with a precise request. Reporter acceptance is mandatory for issues 22 and 25. Issue 32 requires a deterministic reproduction or proof of the exact invalid state. Other internal work may continue, but the affected issue and final plan endpoint remain blocked.
ownerDecisions.rationale: External latency must not weaken evidence or halt unrelated audits and repairs.

ownerDecisions.question: What target versions and support branches own the completed work?
ownerDecisions.selectedChoice: All Forge 1.20.1 fixes, issue 33, and Forge audit repairs ship together as exactly 3.0.0-beta.2 on the 1.20.1 branch. NeoForge issue 22 ships as exactly 2.2.1 on the 1.21.1 branch. No per bug version increment and no cross branch merge.
ownerDecisions.rationale: The two supported runtimes have independent compatibility and release histories.

ownerDecisions.question: Which whole codebase audits are mandatory before completion?
ownerDecisions.selectedChoice: Complete and repair security and privacy, every admin command and permission path, every persistence and database path, and backend integration and failure handling across all named marketplace, economy, escrow, ATM, claim, lifecycle, networking, restart, reconnect, and multiplayer workflows. Every discovered defect is filed before repair and each audit reruns clean at the exact candidate revisions.
ownerDecisions.rationale: Known reports cross trust, persistence, transaction, and lifecycle boundaries and require systematic closure.

externalPrerequisites.name: Issue 22 reporter acceptance on the affected NeoForge 1.21.1 Windows client environment
required_evidence: The reporter tests a JAR built from the exact merged 1.21.1 candidate revision in the originally affected client environment.
The reporter confirms with a screenshot or concise result that the affected FutureShops screens no longer apply unintended background blur and that navigation remains usable.
The issue records the tested version, candidate revision, loader version, Minecraft version, operating system, and result before closure.

externalPrerequisites.name: Issue 25 affected world evidence and reporter acceptance on Forge 1.20.1
required_evidence: A sanitized backup or exact inventory of the affected catalog files, relevant configuration, loader and mod versions, startup and first failure logs, and steps that reproduce unavailable offers after update.

The reporter retests a JAR built from the exact merged Forge candidate revision against a preserved copy of the affected world and confirms offers are available after startup, restart, and catalog reload without data deletion.
The issue records the candidate revision, tested environment, migrated file state, result, and any remaining warning before closure.

externalPrerequisites.name: Exact issue 32 invalid player data evidence or deterministic reproduction
required_evidence: Either a sanitized preserved copy of the affected player data with matching world and FutureShops persistence context, or a deterministic fixture that reproduces the same unusable player state twice without deleting data.
A before and after state report identifies the exact invalid field, ownership transition, persistence write, or recovery mismatch and proves unrelated player data remains unchanged.
The fixed candidate loads and recovers the preserved or reproduced state across restart, reconnect, and repeated transaction attempts without data deletion, duplication, or value loss.

externalPrerequisites.name: Controlled isolated Forge 1.20.1 multiplayer verification environment
required_evidence: An isolated dedicated Forge 1.20.1 server running the exact candidate revision with at least two independent clients and reproducible finite and infinite stock shop fixtures.

Captured server and client logs, balances, inventory states, stock states, request identities, claims, escrow and persistence state for purchase success, rejection, disconnect, retry, restart, and reconnect workflows.
A conservation report proves no duplicated or lost item or currency and no unexpected maintenance, recovery, or module readiness state.

externalPrerequisites.name: Authenticated EnVisione GitHub access for issue, branch, pull request, check, and closure synchronization
required_evidence: The authenticated GitHub identity is EnVisione and the remote resolves to MCEnvision/FutureShops.
Each discovered defect has a duplicate search record, issue link, implementation link, evidence link, and final closure state.
Each support branch and integration pull request reports the required green checks at the exact merged revision.

completionEndpoint: Every scoped open issue, currently issues 22, 25, 32, 33, and 34, plus every repository owned defect verified during the rolling audit, is deduplicated, fixed, regression tested, merged into the correct 1.20.1 or 1.21.1 support branch, supported by mandatory reporter acceptance or exact deterministic reproduction evidence, and closed. Both exact candidate revisions pass the complete security, privacy, command, persistence, integration, runtime, documentation, and repeated clean audit gates, all required branches and checks are green, and the validated Forge 3.0.0-beta.2 and NeoForge 2.2.1 artifacts are prepared with integrity evidence. CurseForge, Modrinth, GitHub release publication, stable publication, and announcements are not part of this endpoint and require later explicit authorization.
